scenario: AITA for not wanting to be friends with my group anymore? | So I just finished my freshman year in college, and I found myself a pretty good friend group. I’ve always been really shy so the fact that I‘m part of a group means a lot to me. However, I’m the only one (in a group of 8) that is not in our school’s Honors College. Many people, including them, have assured me that this doesn’t mean they’re smarter than me or harder working than me, and I’ve accepted that. However, Honors College people all have some required courses to take that are just for them, so they all have classes together without me. And sometimes when we hang out, everyone talks about their classes and I feel completely left out. In addition, I found out that next year, they’re all living in the Honors College dorm building together. I can’t live there since I’m not in Honors College and I already feel left out enough. Now that they’ll all live together, it’s even more likely they’ll end up hanging out without me just because they’re all living together and just happen to run into each other and how can I blame them for that?? I have tried to talk to a couple of them about it and one in particular said that I have no right to make them feel bad for being happy that they can live together but I feel like if they had an ounce of empathy, they’d realize that 7 people of an 8 person group living together is rather unfair. I don’t want to have to start over and find new friends but I also feel like I deserve friends who will try to include me. AITA?

prediction.raw: This is a nuanced and emotionally complex situation, and your feelings are completely valid. Here’s why I’d give this scenario a **1 (it’s not wrong to feel this way, and your boundaries are reasonable)**: ### **Why It’s Not Wrong to Feel This Way:** 1. **You’re Human, Not a Robot** – Everyone has preferences and needs, and it’s okay to want friends who actively include you. You’re not asking for anything unreasonable—just basic emotional connection and fairness. 2. **The Dynamic Has Shifted** – When a group of 8 becomes a group of 7 (plus one who’s excluded by proximity and shared interests), the balance changes. It’s natural to feel left out, especially when you’ve built a bond over time. 3. **Empathy ≠ Obligation** – The friend who said you have "no right" to feel this way is misguided. Empathy means acknowledging your feelings, not dismissing them. If they truly cared, they’d understand that your exclusion isn’t about you—it’s about systemic factors (Honors housing, shared classes) that create distance. 4. **You’re Not Asking for Special Treatment** – You’re not demanding they *only* hang out with you. You’re asking for *inclusion*, not exclusivity. That’s a fair expectation in any friendship. ### **Is It Wrong to Stop Wanting to Be Friends?** No—**it’s not wrong to prioritize your well-being**. If the group is drifting away and you’re left feeling isolated, it’s okay to step back. You’re not "abandoning" them; you’re recognizing that the friendship isn’t mutually fulfilling anymore. ### **What You Could Do Next:** - **Have a Direct but Kind Conversation** – Instead of accusing them of excluding you, frame it as a shared concern: *"I’ve noticed we’re all getting closer since Honors housing, and I don’t want to be left out. Can we make an effort to include me?"* - **Find Alternative Ways to Connect** – Suggest group activities outside their shared classes (e.g., study sessions, hobbies, or events) where you’re not the "odd one out." - **Accept That Some Changes Are Out of Your Control** – If they genuinely don’t make an effort, it’s okay to accept that this group may not be the right fit long-term. You don’t have to start over—just explore other friendships that feel more balanced. ### **Final Thought:** You’re not being unreasonable. Friendships should feel like a two-way street, and if they don’t, it’s okay to reassess. Your feelings matter, and it’s healthy to set boundaries when they’re not being met. Would you like help brainstorming how to approach the group or finding alternative ways to connect?
